subtopics.title: How Paper 1 Is Built and How Marks Are Won

questions.question: Question 1 of Paper 1 is always:
options: About 30 marks of Level 1 questions only, from Finance and Data Handling
The hardest question, saved for strong candidates

questions.question: Paper 1's topic weighting is roughly:
Unfamiliar contexts may appear:
The consistent-accuracy principle means:
options: Later stages still pay when a wrong earlier value is carried forward correctly — so finish the chain

questions.question: VAT at 15% on a R240,00 jersey, for two marks:
Gross salary R15 800,00, deductions R3 240,00. Net pay:
options: R12 560,00 — net is what remains after deductions

questions.question: Even on two-mark items, working is written because:
options: A slip beside visible method usually keeps one mark; a slip with no working forfeits both

questions.question: Water tariff: first 6 kl free; 7–15 kl at R18,00; 16–30 kl at R26,00. For 22 kl, the charged blocks are:
options: 16 kl at R18,00 and 6 kl at R26,00

questions.question: The bill including VAT on the R344,00 subtotal:
options: R344,00 — municipal water carries no VAT

questions.question: Writing the line '6 kl at R0,00' earns a mark because:
options: It proves the block logic — the free block still consumes 6 of the 22 kilolitres

questions.question: The classic tariff error is:
options: Charging all 22 kl at the top rate because 22 falls in that block's range — the table is a staircase, not a switch

subtopics.title: Question 2.2: Compound Interest on a Fixed Deposit

questions.question: R12 000,00 at 8,5% compounded annually: the end of year one is:
After three years the deposit is worth:
options: R15 327,47 — each year's 1,085 applied to the NEW balance

questions.question: The interest earned over the term:
options: R3 327,47 — final value minus the original deposit

questions.question: Against simple interest at the same rate, compound wins by R267,47 because:
options: The bank charges simple savers a fee
Simple interest runs for fewer years
From year two onward, compound interest is calculated on a balance that already contains interest

questions.question: Twelve arranged marks with sum 708: the mean is:
With twelve values, the median is:
options: The average of the sixth and seventh values — (56 + 60) ÷ 2 = 58,0

questions.question: Q1 = 49,0 and Q3 = 69,0, so the interquartile range is:
options: 20 — the spread of the middle half, untouched by the 38 and the 83

questions.question: Commenting on 'the class did well because the mean is 59' earns marks by:
options: Citing computed values — mean 59 near median 58, yet a quarter of the class below Q1 = 49

subtopics.title: Question 4: Integrated Finance, Data and Probability

questions.question: Three of the twelve learners scored below 50%. P(a randomly chosen learner scored below 50%):
options: 3/12 = 1/4 = 0,25 = 25% — any dialect unless one is demanded

questions.question: 200 packets bought at R6,50 and all sold at R10,00 gives a profit of:
options: R700,00 — income R2 000,00 minus costs R1 300,00

questions.question: If only 85% of the 200 packets sell, profit becomes:
options: R400,00 — 170 × R10,00 = R1 700,00 income against the full R1 300,00 cost

questions.question: To clear a R650,00 profit target on 170 sales, the price must round UP to R11,48 because:
options: R11,47 × 170 banks only R1 949,90 — ten cents short of the R1 950,00 needed

questions.question: The method mark is banked the moment:
options: Correct values sit inside a correct structure on paper — like 344 × 1,15 written down

questions.question: On suspecting a slip mid-question, the right move is:
options: Stop and leave the rest blank
Carry the value forward and finish — consistent accuracy keeps paying the later stages

questions.question: Money answers take the form:
options: Rand sign, two decimals, decimal comma — R395,60

questions.question: The quiet mark-killer in long chains is:
options: Premature rounding mid-chain — keep full figures until the final line
